title: The Apprentice star 'was reprimanded by bosses after being accused of using racist language during a task' before dramatically quitting the show
text:

It was thought that the cosmetic dentist, Dr. Jana Denzel, had used the term “Colorado” to describe a black person during a task.
Mailonline revealed Thursday that Jana decided to give up the process, to the shock of Lord Alan Sugar, with her scheduled exit to broadcast in an upcoming episode.
The sources have now said The sun It was reported that before deciding to leave Jana’s comment to show the bosses that they made him undergo diversity training. The BBC insisted on Thursday that its departure was not related to this incident.

Dr. Jana, who has talked about her pride in her heritage of Sri Lanka and refugee parents, sat in discussions with the producers to ensure that she understood the offensive nature of the comment.
It is believed that apprentice viewers will not see their comment on the screen, but their departure will be broadcast during episode five in two weeks.
A BBC spokesman told the publication: ‘Jana retired for completely unrelated and separate reasons, and has all our support.
‘They informed us a poorly informed comment. As soon as it was marked, we take quick and comprehensive measures to address the problem.
‘While we have made Jana very clear that its use of language was not acceptable, we are sure that there was no bad attempt behind him. The concerns of all the parties involved have been addressed and resolved.

The program has a story of candidates who renounce before being fired.
In 2023, Shannon Martin left the process, telling Lord Sugar in the boardroom: “I just don’t think it’s the environment for me.”
During the same season, Donnelly Reece was eliminated from the competition after breaking the rules of the show drinking alcohol on a flight to Dubai.

She said: ‘Mentally, it was strong enough to continue. But my body did not allow me to continue. So I had no choice but to make a difficult decision like that.
Last year, the apprentice was involved in a row of races when Shazia Hussain said she was racially intimidated during her time in the program.
The contestant of reality, Shazia, 40, said that her problems began after she named a yogita giraffe for a preschool cartoon during a task under a topic of diversity and inclusion.
However, he insists that some people in his team fought with the animal’s name, saying that young children could not pronounce it.
She told The Sun: ‘I felt exposed to aggression for that. I think it was racist ‘
While his team won the task, he added: ‘After the episode, I feel that some of the candidates abused me verbally.
‘They (the BBC) brought a diversity specialist to talk to everyone, but I feel that nothing changed. The teams were also reorganized, but I think intimidation continued.
‘I feel that I was intimidated and harassed to the point that I asked to leave the house. I feel that the BBC has failed me.
He added that he complained about the three candidates involved, but has not heard anything else, and added that he thought he was fired after the fifth task “because it was easier to get me out of the situation.”
Shazia said she believes that the BBC did not follow her duty to take care of her.
An apprentice spokesman told the publication: “The apprentice has a zero tolerance policy about any type of intimidation or threatening behavior.”
‘As soon as Shazia raised a concern, an investigation was conducted and received support in person of high -level members of the production team.
‘The apprentice has a strict code of conduct and we take all complaints very seriously and investigate when necessary. As a result, when action is required, we take it.
‘Throughout the process there is always someone available to treat any concern, including five members of the production team living in the house with candidates during filming.
‘If someone wants to leave the house or the process, the candidates are free to do so at any time.
‘Since the beginning of the process, Shazia, together with all other candidates, has been, and continues to be, offered extensive and continuous support, in all aspects of well -being (including the management of social networks), of the BBC and The production company.
“The duty of care with all our candidates is our highest priority and the support offered to candidates before, during and then it is essential.”
